title: Quarterly orchestration for hosted inference & model shelf: release channels, OKR mapping, and cadence
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: define a lightweight, repeatable quarterly orchestration that maps product OKRs to concrete release channels for the hosted API and the model shelf (our internal term for the model catalog). Deliver a plan and automation checklist so engineering, infra, and support can coordinate model rotates, performance rollouts, and capacity commitments without ad-hoc firefighting.
goals: Create a repeatable release-channel taxonomy (gold/beta/edge) for hosted models and model shelf entries
Link 3 top-level OKRs to explicit deliverables and owners for the quarter
Reduce unclear handoffs during model rollouts by 60% (measured via post-release incidents and handoff tasks)
Document a lightweight cadence for staging -> canary -> general rollout and tie automatic metrics gates to each phase
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy doc published and reviewed by Eng/Runtime/Console/Support
Release playbook checked into Confluence with step-by-step rollback and fallback rules
Two pilot model rotations executed on the new channel flow (staging -> canary -> gold) with monitored metrics and no critical incidents
OKR mapping table published and accepted by PM leadership
milestones: 2026-03-08: Draft release-channel taxonomy and mapping matrix
2026-03-15: Stakeholder review workshop (Eng, Runtime, Console, SRE, Support)
2026-03-29: Pilot rotation A (latency-optimized model) through the channel flow
2026-04-12: Pilot rotation B (quantized variant) and retrospective
2026-04-15: Ship playbook and bake into cycle planning templates
risks: Model quality regression during canary stages could trigger customer-visible defects
Cross-team bandwidth misalignments leading to delayed rollouts
Insufficient telemetry gating causing rollouts to proceed without required signal
Ambiguity in ownership for rollback/incident response
mitigation_plans: Require a minimal eval-suite and smoke metrics before canary promotion
Reserve a cross-functional coordination slot in weekly release sync and a named on-call owner for each pilot
Add mandatory pre-promote automated checks in CI that block progression if thresholds fail
Document explicit rollback steps and who executes them (SRE for infra, Runtime for model swap, PM for communications)
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Initial draft taxonomy circulated; runtime team requested clearer gating definitions
2026-03-09: Added automation checklist items after SRE review — pre-promote smoke tests and explicit rollback triggers
2026-03-12: Console team proposed UI affordances for release lanes (filters, labels) — design spike scheduled
2026-03-15: Stakeholder workshop scheduled; pilots identified (latency-optimized v1, quantized v2)
review_feedback: SRE: emphasize concrete thresholds (p50/p95 latency, error-rate) and an emergency cutoff for canary
Runtime Eng: ask for a KV-cache warmup step to be included in staging
Support: request a pre-rollout customer communication template and runbook snippet
Console PM: recommend a per-route visual indicator for channel state (staging/canary/gold)
next_steps: Finalize gating metric definitions and add to the automation checklist
Create two pilot tickets for engineering to run the pilot model rotations
Add release-lane labels to Console backlog and wire UI spike with design
Schedule pilot run dates with SRE and Data & Eval teams
release_plan: Phase 0 (staging): deploy model to isolated pool, run eval-suite, smoke metrics
Phase 1 (canary): 5% traffic, telemetry gates active, 24h minimum observation
Phase 2 (gold): scaled to target capacity with rolling migration and capacity checks
Fallback: automatic downgrade to previous variant on threshold breach with alerting and incident queueing
metrics: OKR-1: Decrease post-deploy incidents related to model rotations by 60% this quarter
OKR-2: 95% of model promotions pass automated gate within 2 hours
Operational: median canary duration under 36 hours for successful promotions
Cost: no more than 12% transient capacity spike during pilot rollouts
notes: This ticket intentionally uses the term 'model shelf' to separate operational catalog concerns from marketing naming
Keep playbook lightweight — the goal is a shim that teams adopt, not a heavy process burden
Coordinate with legal/compliance if any pilot models touch regulated PII customers
